extracted.intended_audience: State air pollution control agencies; owners/operators of affected EGUs preparing State plans under the EPA Carbon Pollution Standards
extracted.subtask_short: State plan for EGU carbon standards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory elements that States must include in State plans to implement the EPA's Carbon Pollution Standards for affected electric generating units (EGUs), including data inventories, standards of performance, increments of progress, reporting, and mechanisms for extensions or reliability exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcategory definitions by fuel type and capacity factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines subcategories such as base load, intermediate load, and low load for oil-fired and natural gas-fired steam generating units based on annual capacity factor thresholds (>=45%, >=8% and <45%, <8%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these capacity-factor thresholds to classify affected EGUs into the correct subcategory for purposes of standards, applicability, and required State plan elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory of data from affected EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: State plan must include an inventory of the following data from the affected EGUs: (i) nameplate capacity as defined in §60.5880b; (ii) base load rating as defined in §60.5880b; (iii) data within the continuous 5-year period immediately prior to May 9, 2024 including: (A) sum of CO2 emissions during each quarter in the 5-year period; (B) for all subcategories except low-load natural gas and oil, the sum of gross energy output during each quarter; for low-load natural gas and oil subcategories, the sum of heat input during each quarter; (C) heat input for each fuel type combusted during each quarter; (D) start and end dates of the most representative continuous 8-quarter period used to determine the baseline under §60.5775b(d), the sum of CO2 mass emissions during that period, the sum of gross energy output or heat input during that period, and sum of heat input for each fuel type during that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the complete quarterly and representative-period data exactly as specified to support baseline calculations and subcategory determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of performance for each affected EGU
rubrics_metrics.description: State plan must include all standards of performance for each affected EGU according to §60.5775b. Standards of performance must be established at a level of performance that does not exceed the level calculated through the methods described in §60.5775b(b), unless a State establishes a standard pursuant to §60.5775b(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each affected EGU has an explicit standard of performance in the State plan that is consistent with §60.5775b methodology or justified under §60.5775b(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements related to subcategory applicability (enforceable requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: State plan must include enforceable requirements to establish an affected EGU's applicability for subcategories, including: (A) medium-term coal-fired units must permanently cease operations by a date after Dec 31, 2031 and before Jan 1, 2039; (B) units that are natural gas- or oil-fired but retain coal-firing capability or fired coal in prior 5 years or will fire coal before Jan 1, 2030 must remove coal-firing capability before Jan 1, 2030; (C) estimate coal, oil, and natural gas usage by heat input for first 3 calendar years after Jan 1, 2030 for each affected EGU; (D) units planning to permanently cease operation must comply with applicable State and Federal requirements for permanent cessation, including removal from State air emissions inventory and amending/revoking permits to reflect permanent shutdown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include enforceable requirements and supporting documentation demonstrating removals, cessation dates, and fuel-use estimates as applicable to establish correct subcategory applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increments of progress (required elements for long-term and medium-term coal-fired subcategories)
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include legally enforceable increments of progress for affected EGUs in the long-term coal-fired and medium-term coal-fired subcategories. For units using CCS (long-term) or natural gas co-firing (medium-term), assign calendar-date deadlines to each increment and meet website posting obligations. Required increments include: (A) submittal of a final control plan with supporting analysis (FEED for long-term; design basis, timeline, benchmarks for medium-term); (B) completion of awarding of contracts (with examples for each subcategory); (C) initiation of on-site construction or installation (90% carbon capture annual basis for long-term; boiler modifications for 40% co-firing annual average for medium-term); (D) completion of on-site construction or installation (same performance targets as (C)); (E) commencement of permitting actions related to pipeline construction with required supporting documentation; (F) report identifying CO2 injection geographic location, transportation, regulatory requirements, and timeline (long-term CCS units); (G) compliance with the standard of performance by specified dates (medium-term by Jan 1, 2030; long-term by Jan 1, 2032).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign explicit calendar deadlines for each increment, collect the specified supporting documentation, and ensure increments are legally enforceable in the State plan. Post increments and evidence of meeting them on the required website within 30 business days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increments for units using alternate control strategies (per 40 CFR 60.21a(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: For any long-term coal-fired unit meeting its standard by a control other than CCS, or medium-term coal-fired unit using a control other than natural gas co-firing, State plans must include appropriate increments of progress consistent with 40 CFR 60.21a(h). The increment corresponding to 60.21a(h)(1) must be assigned the earliest calendar date; the increment corresponding to 60.21a(h)(5) must be assigned no later than Jan 1, 2032 for long-term and no later than Jan 1, 2030 for medium-term units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map the alternate control strategy to the specific 40 CFR 60.21a(h) increments and assign required calendar dates consistent with the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting and deviation reporting for increments of progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operators must post within 30 business days of State plan submittal a description of activities/actions constituting increments of progress and the schedule on the Carbon Pollution Standards for EGUs website. As calendar dates occur, post documentation demonstrating each increment has been met within 30 business days. The State plan must require owners/operators to report any deviation from any federally enforceable increment of progress to the State regulatory agency within 30 business days after the owner/operator knew or should have known; the report must explain causes and measures to cure and prevent recurrence and include timeframes. Owners/operators must also post any deviation reports on the Carbon Pollution Standards website within 30 business days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain timely public postings and internal/submitted deviation reports with full explanation and corrective plans; include timeframes for cures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting obligations and milestones for EGUs planning permanent cessation
rubrics_metrics.description: State plan must include legally enforceable reporting obligations/milestones for medium-term coal-fired units and EGUs invoking RULOF for remaining useful life. Requirements include: (i) Initial Milestone Report five years before planned permanent cessation or 60 days after State plan submission (whichever later) containing (A) summary of process steps and timing to permanently cease operations, (B) list of key milestones and calendar deadlines (must include initial notice to reliability authority and retirement filing), (C) analysis comparing timelines to similar EGUs that ceased within prior 10 years, (D) supporting regulatory documents (correspondence/filings with RTO/ISOs/PUCs, deactivation-related reliability assessments, SEC filings or investor notices including 10-K/10-Q references, integrated resource plans, reliability analyses, notifications altering timing). (ii) Annual Milestone Status Reports for each remaining year prior to cessation documenting progress and supporting documents. (iii) Final Milestone Status Report no later than six months after permanent cessation documenting actions to ensure permanence. (iv) Posting of all reports on Carbon Pollution Standards website within 30 business days of filing. (v) Deviation reporting to State agency and posting of deviation report within 30 business days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full documentary support (regulatory filings, reliability assessments, SEC references) and year-by-year milestone progress; post publicly within required timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, reporting, and recordkeeping requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: State plan must include all applicable monitoring, reporting and recordkeeping requirements, including initial and ongoing quality assurance and quality control procedures, for each affected EGU, and the requirements must be consistent with or no less stringent than §60.5860b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt monitoring/QA/QC/reporting protocols at least as stringent as §60.5860b and include them as enforceable State-plan requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: State reporting to EPA about State plan implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: State plan must include a description of the process, contents, and schedule for State reporting to the EPA about State plan implementation and progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify what the State will report to EPA, the format/content, frequency, and schedule for submission to enable EPA oversight of State plan implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific requirements for existing coal-fired steam generating EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: State plan must require: (i) any existing coal-fired steam-generating EGU shall operate only subject to a standard of performance pursuant to §60.5775b or under an exemption of applicability provided under §60.5850b (including extensions per the reliability assurance mechanism); (ii) include a list of coal-fired steam generating EGUs that are existing sources at time of State plan submission that plan to permanently cease operation before Jan 1, 2032, with calendar dates for cessation; (iii) provide that an existing coal-fired EGU operating past the date listed in the State plan is in violation, except to the extent it has received an extension pursuant to the reliability assurance mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and date all existing coal-fired EGUs that intend to cease by 2032 and ensure enforceability; define violation status for operation past listed dates unless an approved extension applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon Pollution Standards for EGUs website requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: State plan must require owners/operators to establish a publicly accessible 'Carbon Pollution Standards for EGUs Website' and post relevant documents: subcategory designations, compliance schedules, emissions data and other information needed to demonstrate compliance, information relevant to increments of progress and reporting obligations including milestones for EGUs planning permanent cessation, and any extension requests and approvals. Data should be available in a readily downloadable format. The State must establish a website that displays links to these owner/operator websites for all affected EGUs in the State plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely posting of data and documents in downloadable formats and maintain a State-level index of links to EGU sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance date extension mechanism (optional State provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans may include provisions allowing an owner/operator of affected EGUs installing add-on controls to request a compliance date extension up to one year (only once) if unable to meet the compliance date due to circumstances beyond their control. An extension request must contain a demonstration of necessity including: (A) identification of each affected unit; (B) description of controls to be installed; (C) description/demonstration of progress toward installing controls including contracts and permits (or applications and anticipated permit timeframes); (D) identification of circumstances beyond control necessitating extra time (evidence from vendors/engineering firms, permit delays, infrastructure delays such as CO2 pipelines); (E) proposed compliance date no later than one year after the applicable compliance date and updated increment calendar dates. The State air pollution control agency approves/disapproves extension requests based on completeness and demonstrations. Approval provisions must include deadlines for submission (no later than 6 months prior to applicable compliance date), EPA Regional Administrator notification, posting of application and State determination on the Carbon Pollution Standards website, and updating website information within 30 days if approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If including an extension mechanism, incorporate the full set of submission, documentation, notification, and posting requirements and deadlines to ensure transparent, auditable extension decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term reliability mechanism components
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans may include a short-term reliability mechanism for affected EGUs operating during a system emergency (as defined in §60.5880b). Components must include: (i) availability only during system emergencies and identification of entity/entities authorized to issue system emergencies; (ii) provision that during a documented system emergency an impacted EGU may comply with an emission limitation equal to its baseline emission performance rate (calculated under §60.5775b(d)) in lieu of its otherwise applicable standard of performance; (iii) documentation required to demonstrate the system emergency and that the EGU was impacted, including documentation that the system emergency was in effect, that it included the source/region, instruction to increase output or remain in operation, and data collected during the event (sum CO2, sum gross energy output, resulting CO2 performance rate); (iv) requirement to document hours an affected EGU operated under a system emergency and which emission limitation applied; (v) provision that, for compliance demonstration, the affected EGU would comply with its baseline emissions rate for the hours corresponding to the event; (vi) requirement that defining provisions be part of the public comment process for the State plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit use to documented system emergencies with required agency authorization and collect detailed operational and emissions data for each event; include mechanism language in public process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability assurance mechanism (extensions for grid reliability)
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans may include a reliability assurance mechanism allowing one extension (not to exceed 12 months) of a planned permanent cessation date where operation is necessary for electric grid reliability. Applicability is limited to eligible EGUs (certain coal-fired exempt units, medium-term coal units with enforceable commitments to cease before Jan 1, 2039, and EGUs with enforceable dates under §60.24a(g)). Requirements include: extension runs from the State plan cessation date; extension only available after satisfying all applicable increments of progress and reporting obligations; applicable standard of performance remains in place during extension; extensions up to 6 months are considered by EPA Regional Administrator (submission at least 30 days prior to cease date, no earlier than 12 months prior) and extensions >6 to ≤12 months require submission to FERC and EPA Regional Administrator (submitted no less than 45 days prior to cease date, but no earlier than 12 months prior); application content for ≤6 months includes: (A) reliability-risk analysis demonstrating criticality and length of need (must show it would cause FERC-mandated reliability violations or increased loss of load expectation), (B) certification from relevant reliability planning authority with substantiating analysis, (C) copies of any written comments from third parties, (D) demonstration plan to bring on new capacity or transmission including steps and timeframes, (E) other requested information; application process limits (extensions only for substantiated period, ≤12 months total, may not be used more than once), and EPA may reject incomplete or unsupported submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide robust, certified reliability analyses and supporting documentation; adhere to submission timelines and filing routes depending on extension length; ensure all increments and reporting obligations are satisfied before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable forms of standards of performance (§60.5775b(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard of performance for an affected EGU may take the following forms: (1) a rate-based standard of performance for an individual affected EGU that does not exceed the level calculated through methods in §60.5775b(c) and (d); (2) a standard of performance in an alternate form, which may apply for affected EGUs in the long-term or medium-term coal-fired subcategories, as provided for in §60.5775b(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans must specify whether each unit's standard is rate-based or an allowable alternate form and demonstrate conformity with the relevant §60.5775b subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required characteristics of standards of performance (§60.5775b(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of performance included under a State plan must be demonstrated to be quantifiable, verifiable, non-duplicative, permanent, and enforceable with respect to each affected EGU. The State plan must include methods by which each standard meets each requirement: (1) quantifiable if it can be reliably measured and replicated; (2) verifiable if adequate monitoring, recordkeeping and reporting are in place to enable independent evaluation; (3) non-duplicative if not already incorporated as a standard in the State plan; (4) permanent if met continuously unless replaced by another approved standard; (5) enforceable if (i) a technically accurate limitation and time period are specified, (ii) compliance requirements are clearly defined, (iii) affected EGUs are responsible and liable for violations, (iv) each compliance activity/measure is enforceable as a practical matter (40 CFR 49.167), and (v) Administrator, State, and third parties maintain ability to enforce and secure corrective actions under the CAA (sections cited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly document how each standard is measurable, supported by monitoring/recordkeeping/reporting, not duplicative, continuously applicable, and legally enforceable with clear compliance obligations and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for presumptively approvable standards of performance (long-term and medium-term coal-fired units)
rubrics_metrics.description: For presumptively approvable standards: (1) Long-term coal-fired steam generating units: BSER is CCS with 90 percent capture of CO2; degree of emission limitation is 88.4 percent reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh‑gross); presumptively approvable standard is an emission rate limit defined by an 88.4 percent reduction in annual emission rate from the unit-specific baseline. (2) Medium-term coal-fired steam generating units: BSER is natural gas co-firing at 40 percent of the heat input to the unit; degree of emission limitation is a 16 percent reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh‑gross); presumptively approvable standard is an emission rate limit defined by a 16 percent reduction in annual emission rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing presumptively approvable standards for units in these subcategories, apply the specified BSERs and percent reductions relative to unit-specific baselines and document calculations.
